topics: Continuous batching and batch size tuning
KV cache warm-up and prefix caching
transcript: Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Ava Chen (Redwood AE), Mateo Ruiz (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (BrightPath Head of ML), Carlos Mendes (BrightPath Infra), Elena Park (BrightPath PM)
[00:00] Ava Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining the weekly sync. quick sanity check, is this still the same throughput target 1800 reqs per second with p95 latency under 300ms?
[00:08] Priya Patel: yes, that's the target for peak, um, we also have a soft goal of 1.5x for burst capacity during spikes

[00:14] Mateo Ruiz: cool, we ran a couple of runs overnight — i'll go through the numbers; quick note, logs are in the shared folder but the naming got a little funky so like look for 'brp-throughput-11-12'.
[00:26] Carlos Mendes: yeah we saw those, thanks. good to know on the filename, we had a quick parsing error but fixed it locally

[00:32] Mateo Ruiz: alright so baseline: with default batching we hit about 1,250 reqs/sec sustained, p95 around 220ms for a 512-token average payload. when we enabled continuous batching with target_batch_size 64 and aggressive batch timeout 6ms, we pushed to ~1,780 reqs/sec but saw p95 jump to mid-300s intermittently
[00:54] Priya Patel: ok that p95 jump is concerning, is that because of queueing inside the runtime or client concurrency spikes?

[01:00] Mateo Ruiz: it's a mix — the runtime's batching introduces some queueing delay under bursty arrival patterns. we also hit GPU concurrency limits at times which caused small stalls and head-of-line blocking for a few sequences
[01:12] Ava Chen: are you using prefix/KV caching for these runs? i remember the first week you weren't warming the cache which hit repeat token cost
[01:18] Priya Patel: we turned on prefix caching last week but warming is incomplete; we only had about 40% of common prefixes cached during the run

[01:24] Mateo Ruiz: yep, KV cache warm-up is important — with warm cache we saw per-token latency drop ~10-15% which helps p95. but cold-cache misses exacerbate the queueing because misses take longer and hold batch slots
[01:36] Elena Park: quick question — what do you mean by 'aggressive batch timeout 6ms'? is that a server-side param or part of the SDK?

[01:42] Mateo Ruiz: it's runtime config. Greenwood — sorry, redwood runtime — exposes a batch_timeout and target_batch_size; lower timeout reduces latency but risks underfilled batches, higher timeout increases utilization. we set it to 6ms to force filling batches quickly for throughput tests
[01:55] Priya Patel: hmm okay. so what's the sweet spot? do we need client-side rate limiting to smooth arrivals?

[02:02] Mateo Ruiz: yeah, client-side concurrency capping + a small client queue helps. in our tests, limiting concurrent inflight per-client to ~500 and letting the runtime batch to 64 produced stable throughput without huge p95 spikes
[02:14] Carlos Mendes: is there a recommended queueing strategy? token-based, request-based? we have mixed payload sizes (avg 512 but some up to 1024).

[02:22] Mateo Ruiz: request-concurrency cap is easier operationally. you can also weight by token length; another approach is rate-limiter + leaky bucket at the edge to smooth bursts. we can share a config snippet for the SDK
[02:33] Ava Chen: action: Mateo will share recommended SDK config and a script to run the sustained test — agreed?
[02:36] Priya Patel: yes please
[02:38] Mateo Ruiz: i'll include a sample that does a warm-up phase to prefill KV cache — we found 10-15 minutes of warm traffic covers most common prefixes
[02:46] Elena Park: 10-15 minutes of warm-up, noted. for the customer infra side, do we need persistent storage for cache or is it kept only in-GPU?

[02:53] Mateo Ruiz: the KV cache is kept in-memory on the serving nodes (GPU host memory + GPU memory mappings), it's ephemeral to the serving instance. for Dedicated/Private we can do sticky routing so the same session hits warmed nodes; otherwise we recommend pre-warming before major traffic windows
[03:07] Priya Patel: sticky routing could be tricky with our autoscale. any suggestions?

[03:11] Mateo Ruiz: you can use session affinity for bursts, or maintain a small pool of 'warm' nodes that handle repeat traffic; Redwood's routing supports policies for this — we can go deeper if you plan a production rollout
[03:21] Carlos Mendes: on the GPU stalls you mentioned, is that queuing on the host or contention on kernel launches? we saw periods where GPU util dropped briefly

[03:28] Mateo Ruiz: those were kernel launch contention plus small GC-ish pauses when memory fragmentation triggered a host-side compaction. we reduced those by tuning allocator settings and aligning batch sizes to multiples of 32 tokens which reduces fragmentation
[03:41] Priya Patel: aligning to multiples of 32 — interesting, we hadn't considered that. any perf tradeoffs?

[03:45] Mateo Ruiz: negligible for throughput, but it improves tail latency consistency. also quantization profile matters; we did a low-precision run (4-bit) and saw 20-30% throughput gains but a slight quality delta on some prompts
[03:58] Priya Patel: quality delta — can you surface which prompts regressed? we need to evaluate against our eval set
[04:02] Mateo Ruiz: sure, i'll attach the eval diff for the quantized run. note that for many workloads 4-bit is fine but for clinical or regulated text you may prefer 8-bit or FP16
[04:12] Ava Chen: this is where the Optimize recommendations help — model-level quantization suggestions tied to your evals. we'll include those notes in the follow-up
[04:18] Elena Park: returning to queuing — do you have guidance for backpressure? what should the client do when queue depth grows?

[04:23] Mateo Ruiz: best practice is to implement client-side bounded queue and fail-fast or provisionally degrade non-critical traffic into lower-priority route. Redwood supports per-route priorities and automatic fallback to cheaper model variants under high load
[04:35] Priya Patel: we like the fallback idea for non-core flows. for core patient-facing flows we need hard SLOs though
[04:40] Ava Chen: understood — for those we recommend Dedicated capacity or reserved warm nodes with strict routing. that avoids noisy neighbors and preserves warmed caches
[04:48] Carlos Mendes: what about networking — we saw occasional network spikes adding ~10-20ms, could that be causing p95 blips?
[04:54] Mateo Ruiz: yes, egress and cross-AZ hops can add variability. for tighter SLOs we suggest colocating inference nodes and reducing cross-host hops; we can map this in the security deep-dive
[05:02] Priya Patel: speaking of the security deep-dive, can you confirm Redwood supports customer KMS/HSM for key management?
[05:07] Ava Chen: yes, we integrate with customer KMS and can do HSM-backed key storage for Private deployments. we'll bring in security docs and a follow-up with our security engineer
[05:16] Priya Patel: perfect, please share compliance artifacts (SOC2, ISO) as well
[05:20] Ava Chen: will do

[05:22] Mateo Ruiz: quick perf note — when we did the 1-hour mixed workload run with client-side concurrency capped at 500 and warm cache, p95 stayed under 280ms at 1.9k reqs/sec. the 2k target is within reach but needs the sustained run to validate stability
[05:36] Priya Patel: ok so the planned 30-minute sustained run at 2k is the next milestone
[05:40] Carlos Mendes: on infra we'll spin up a dedicated test fleet with fixed routing for the run so we don't hit autoscale quirks
[05:46] Mateo Ruiz: perfect. also note we'll enable detailed tracing hooks for that run — expect ~2-3GB of logs; share a log ingestion path
[05:54] Priya Patel: we have an S3 bucket, i'll share credentials with restricted access
[05:58] Ava Chen: great. last thing — pricing. after 3 weeks of pilot if numbers hold we can propose a Dedicated pilot discount. i'll send options
[06:06] Priya Patel: thanks. any blockers from your side?
[06:09] Ava Chen: none right now; just need the traffic profile and greenlight for the 30m run
[06:14] Elena Park: we'll circulate the traffic profile today

[06:17] Ava Chen: awesome. recap: Mateo runs sustained 30m at 2k, share logs; Ava sends pricing; Priya & Carlos share traffic + network diagram; schedule security deep-dive wk of 11/17. any other items?
[06:28] Priya Patel: no, that's it, thanks everyone
[06:30] Ava Chen: thanks all — we'll follow up in thread and update the ticket. bye
[06:33] (call ends)
